lede:
Moving on. Ripple Fire keeps its glyph and stays on an open list — card_batch.py --wanted — because your note was the right one: a picture made for another card may turn out to be its picture. The bank already runs that way in one direction; it now runs in both, and --install will put any banked 92×60 onto any card whatever round it came from.

What Ripple Fire taught this brief

Full Auto was the other card at risk of the handgun read — a close view of a feed mechanism has no more inherent scale than a close view of a gun. So this brief carries a sized by line, which is new, and it does not solve scale with a big foreground object, which is what broke Ripple Fire's second brief.

The advantage this card has, and Ripple Fire never did, is that its second thing is already in the mechanism: the belt goes in and the spent cases come out. That is an actor, a thing acted on, and direction, without importing a starship or a target into a 92×60 frame.

cards.actor: a linked ammunition belt being dragged upward into a breech
cards.on: the spent cases it becomes, falling away out of the bottom of the frame
cards.moment: one continuous motion read in two directions at once: fresh rounds climbing in on the belt, empty brass tumbling out below, the mechanism between them doing the work. Volume as a feed rate rather than as a flash. The belt should run off the top of the frame and the casings off the bottom, so the machine reads as something that has been doing this for a while and is not about to stop.
cards.scale: a gloved crewman's hand or forearm steadying the belt at the edge of frame, or a boot-worn deck grating under the falling brass. One human-sized thing, small and at the margin — enough to say this mechanism is bigger than a person, without becoming the subject the way a starship did.
cards.avoid: the muzzle end and any complete weapon — 'volume as a philosophy' is a feed rate, and the picture is the feed. No large foreground structure: that is what ate the frame on Ripple Fire's second brief. Do not say 'hull', 'vessel' or 'shell' in the prompt; all three have imported an ocean or a rocky floor unprompted.
